question: Assume today is 2026-08-15. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of recreation visits to Yellowstone National Park in August 2026, as it will be reported in the National Park Service's official monthly visitation statistics.

target.what: Recreation visits to Yellowstone National Park as reported in the National Park Service's official monthly visitation statistics. A recreation visit is one person entering the park for recreational purposes; the same person entering multiple times on different days counts as multiple visits.
target.publisher: National Park Service (NPS), typically via the Visitor Use Statistics program (IRMA/NPS Stats).
target.cadence: Monthly, usually published with a lag of several weeks to a few months after the month ends.
target.caveats: The target period is future relative to the 2026-08-15 cutoff. The estimate must rely on historical seasonal patterns, recent partial-year data, and any available signals up to mid-August 2026. The NPS may revise figures; the official reported number is the target. Alternative interpretations: total

candidates.hypothesis: August recreation visits in recent years (2019-2025) provide a baseline for the seasonal peak. The 2026 value is likely to be similar to recent Augusts, adjusted for any known shocks (e.g., 2022 flood, 2020 COVID).
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly recreation visits for Yellowstone National Park for August 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, and 2025. Also, if available, the most recent monthly data for 2026 (e.g., June or July 2026) to gauge the current year's trend.
search_hints: Yellowstone National Park monthly visitation statistics August 2025

candidates.hypothesis: Year-to-date recreation visits through July 2026 can be used to estimate August 2026 by applying the historical share of August in the annual total or the historical ratio of August to July visits.
candidates.data_to_find: Year-to-date recreation visits for Yellowstone for 2026 through July (or June if July not yet available). Also, historical monthly shares: August visits as a percentage of annual total, and August-to-July ratio for recent years.

candidates.perspective: Entrance station counts and vehicle occupancy
candidates.hypothesis: Recreation visits can be estimated from vehicle entries at park entrances multiplied by average occupancy. If entrance counts for August 2026 are available (or can be inferred from recent data), this provides an independent route.
candidates.data_to_find: Number of vehicles entering Yellowstone in August (or recent Augusts) and average persons per vehicle. Alternatively, total vehicle entries for 2026 year-to-date and seasonal patterns.
search_hints: average occupancy Yellowstone visitors per vehicle

candidates.hypothesis: Overnight stays in the park (lodges, campgrounds) plus day-use visits can be used to estimate total recreation visits. Occupancy rates and capacity constraints may limit the maximum possible visits.
candidates.data_to_find: Number of overnight stays in Yellowstone accommodations (lodges, campgrounds) in August, average length of stay, and day-use proportion. Also, total capacity (rooms, campsites) and typical August occupancy.

candidates.hypothesis: Any closures, road construction, wildfires, or policy changes in 2026 could significantly affect August visitation. Identifying such events helps adjust the historical baseline.
candidates.data_to_find: News of Yellowstone closures, road conditions, wildfire impacts, or changes in entry policies in 2026, especially affecting summer months. Also, any reports of record or low visitation in early summer 2026.

candidates.hypothesis: The ratio of August visits to annual visits is relatively stable. Applying this ratio to a forecast of 2026 annual visits (or using recent growth rates) can yield an estimate.
candidates.data_to_find: Historical annual recreation visits for Yellowstone (2015-2025) and the August share each year. Also, any published forecasts for 2026 annual visitation.
search_hints: Yellowstone August share of annual visits

candidates.hypothesis: Online attention (Google Trends, social media mentions) for Yellowstone in summer 2026 may correlate with visitation. If attention is significantly higher or lower than previous years, it could signal a change in visits.
candidates.data_to_find: Google Trends data for 'Yellowstone National Park' for summer 2026 compared to previous summers. Social media post volumes if available.

candidates.hypothesis: Any published forecasts for Yellowstone visitation in 2026 or prediction markets on tourism numbers could provide a direct estimate or a range.
candidates.data_to_find: Reports from tourism boards, economic forecasts for national park visitation, or prediction market contracts on Yellowstone visitation.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
